Before / after

From weak reporting patterns to trusted operating models.

Before

Spreadsheet-based reporting with local logic, fragile joins and hidden manual corrections.

After

Decision-ready reporting backed by governed ingestion, historical modelling and reusable KPI definitions.

This article expands the LinkedIn presentation into a practical framework for People Analytics leaders, practitioners and data teams. It focuses on the choices that make workforce information trusted, explainable and decision-ready.

01 · Deep dive

The reporting trust problem

When teams repeatedly extract, clean and interpret the same records, each report can establish its own population, reference date and KPI logic. Reconciliation becomes recurring work and management attention moves from the decision to a debate about which number is correct.

02 · Deep dive

What an HR DataMart is

An HR DataMart is a decision-oriented analytical layer. It integrates selected operational data, preserves historical context, standardises keys and classifications, applies controls and exposes reusable business definitions. It organises source systems for analysis rather than replacing them.

Apply it

Document the rule, assign an owner, define a threshold or acceptance condition, and specify what users see when the control fails.

03 · Deep dive

Common KPI definitions

Common KPI definitions must be treated as an explicit part of the analytical product, not as an undocumented implementation detail. Define the business purpose, population, time basis, owner, control and failure behaviour. Then connect the rule to evidence that can be reviewed when data, structures or stakeholder expectations change. In the context of why hr reporting should not start with a spreadsheet, this is what makes the outcome reusable, auditable and explainable.

Interactive explainer

Explore the operating logic

Select concepts in sequence and use the flow as a review path for your own analytical product. No employee data is used.

Decision takeaway

Make definitions, time, quality, ownership, access and failure behaviour visible. That is how a data pipeline becomes a trusted decision product.

Executive takeaway

What this means for workforce decision makers.

Spreadsheets are useful delivery tools, but they are unreliable as the foundation for workforce decisions. Build the governed HR DataMart first so every downstream metric has a definition, owner and history.

Key business questions

Questions leaders should ask next.

Which executive decisions are currently supported by spreadsheet-only logic?

Where do metric definitions break when headcount, attrition or movement needs history?

What governance evidence would a CHRO need before trusting the number in a board deck?

Common mistakes

Failure patterns to avoid.

Mistake 1

Starting with report layouts before defining business entities and time logic.

Mistake 2

Treating extracts as controlled history instead of rebuilding from governed source pipelines.

Mistake 3

Publishing KPI packs without showing data quality, ownership or refresh status.

Practical implementation guidance

How to operationalize the idea.

  1. Map the recurring decisions that require workforce evidence.
  2. Define the minimum trusted entities, dates and conformed dimensions behind those decisions.
  3. Create a governed semantic layer so every consuming report inherits the same KPI logic.
